topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
target_audience: University students with basic programming/math knowledge

sections.title: The Problem: Why Traditional Models Fail
lecture_lines: RNNs process words sequentially, causing them to forget context.
Long sentences lose critical connections between distant words.
Human reading allows jumping between related ideas instantly.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Query, Key, and Value
lecture_lines: Think of attention as a library retrieval system.
Query represents what information you are seeking.
Key acts as the index label for a resource.
Value provides the actual content you need.
These three roles structure how Transformers process data.

Show interaction between Query and Key represented by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shelf.svg].

sections.title: The Math: Dot Product and Softmax
lecture_lines: Dot product measures how similar two words are.
High dot product indicates strong contextual relevance.
Softmax normalizes these scores into attention weights.
Weights determine how much 'focus' to apply.
Together, they map out relationships between all words.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Big Picture
lecture_lines: A single attention head limits contextual understanding.
We use multiple heads to process information in parallel.
Each head captures different linguistic features simultaneously.
One head tracks grammar, another detects entities.
Combining them builds a rich, deep understanding.

sections.title: Summary and Application
lecture_lines: Attention mechanism transforms text into mathematical relationships.
It allows models to ignore irrelevant filler words.
This enables efficient processing of massive documents.
